The statement is cautious about near-term growth and inflation due to COVID-19, but it is paired with strong accommodation and forward guidance. The FOMC held the funds rate at 0–0.25%, continued Treasury and agency MBS purchases, and pledged to maintain an accommodative stance until employment and inflation goals are met. However, the Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey indicates headwinds on the credit channel: banks reported, on net, tightening lending standards and terms for C&I loans to firms of all sizes and for CRE loans, alongside weaker demand in these categories during Q3 2020. For households, banks tightened standards for credit card and auto loans (with softer demand), while mortgage demand was stronger but standards generally tighter. Banks cited a deteriorating economic outlook, reduced risk tolerance, and concerns about collateral values and borrower credit quality. These SLOOS findings suggest that, despite supportive monetary policy and improved market functioning, tighter bank lending standards could restrain the flow of credit to more vulnerable borrowers—particularly small firms and CRE—tempering the overall outlook. Net tone: cautious on the outlook with policy support offset by tighter bank credit.
